opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Isaiah promises it.
Jesus announces it.
In Himself, He fulfills it.

And the beautiful part is that the “favor of the Lord” is not abstract. It looks like:
sins forgiven,
the broken restored,
the lost sought out,
the wounded healed,
the poor evangelized,
prisoners released,
and humanity invited back to God.

When Jesus reads Isaiah 61 in Luke 4, He stops after “to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor” and does not continue with “and the day of vengeance of our God.” That is important because it shows what He is emphasizing about His mission.

Jesus is revealing the purpose of His first coming. He came first to bring mercy, healing, repentance, and restoration. He came to save, not to condemn. That does not mean judgment is not real. It means that in this moment, Jesus is announcing that the time of grace has begun.

So the omission is not accidental. Jesus is showing that He is ushering in the long-awaited time of God’s favor. In Him, the promise of Isaiah is being fulfilled. God is now visiting His people with mercy, inviting the poor, broken, captive, and lost back to Himself.

Jesus, I love you.
